events.text: Utterson and Enfield take their Sunday walk down a by-street.
events.quote: It chanced on one of these rambles that their way led them down a by-street

events.text: Enfield points his cane at a sinister door and asks Utterson if he ever remarked it.
events.quote: the former lifted up his cane and pointed

events.text: Enfield says the door is connected with a very odd story.
events.quote: It is connected in my mind

events.text: The man tramples over the girl's body and leaves her screaming.
events.quote: the man trampled calmly over the child’s body and left her screaming on the ground

events.text: Enfield collars the man and brings him back to the group around the child.
events.quote: collared my gentleman, and brought him back

events.text: The doctor turns sick and white with desire to kill the prisoner.
events.quote: I saw that Sawbones turn sick and white with the desire to kill him

events.text: They threaten scandal and force the man to pay a hundred pounds.
events.quote: we screwed him up to a hundred pounds for the child’s family

events.text: The man leads them to the door, unlocks it, and returns with gold and a cheque.
events.quote: whipped out a key, went in, and presently came back

events.text: The man offers to stay until the banks open and cash the cheque himself.
events.quote: I will stay with you till the banks open and cash the cheque myself

events.text: They spend the night in Enfield's chambers and go to the bank next day.
events.quote: passed the rest of the night in my chambers

events.text: Enfield presents the cheque believing it a forgery, but it proves genuine.
